minutes.headline: Commission found no four votes for firearm hunting, approved two forest cutting plans, and sought a land survey.
minutes.summary: The commission heard several wetlands hearings, approving a septic replacement, a retaining wall project and a deck project with conditions, and continuing two others. It authorized forest cutting plan work for the Renault and Hollis Road properties and a survey request on an encroachment. Firearm hunting was debated at length with no vote, and a workshop was tentatively set for January 6.

public_comment.topic: Summarized the letters received, nearly all opposing firearm hunting on conservation land over safety, noise and trust in land purchases.

what_happened.line: The commission authorized its administrator to approach a forester about forest cutting plans for the Renault and Hollis Road properties.
Firearm hunting on conservation land was debated at length with no vote; it returns on the January 20th agenda.
The commission approved a septic replacement, a wall and grading project, and a deck plan with conditions, and continued two other hearings to January 20th.
The chair was authorized to approach town officials about a survey of the 192 Harbor Road encroachment; the commission would ask the selectmen to fund it.
A workshop on land use regulations was tentatively set for January 6th.

why_it_matters: Whether firearm hunting is allowed on town conservation land is still undecided, and most letters received opposed it, so residents near these parcels may want to weigh in before January 20th.

Forest cutting plans would fund parking and trail work from timber revenue before the town receives payment, and the encroachment survey would be asked of the selectmen, so both touch town money and public land access.
watch_next: January 20th meeting: firearm hunting returns to the agenda, along with continued hearings for Lot 1 Page Street, 1672 Mass Avenue and the Five Spring Street tree certification.
January 6th: tentative workshop on land use regulations.
